Tomato Healthy.description: The image most closely resembles the healthy training class. This does not exclude hidden disease, nutrient stress, or a condition outside the five classes.
management: Continue inspecting leaves, stems, and fruit for changes.
Maintain consistent watering at the soil surface.
prevention: Use healthy seed and transplants.
Space and support plants to improve airflow.
Remove crop residue and keep gardening tools clean.

Tomato Early Blight.description: Early blight produces dark brown leaf lesions, often with concentric rings and yellowing, and can affect stems and fruit.
management: Remove affected leaves carefully and clean tools afterward.
Keep foliage dry and water at the base.
Monitor remaining leaves for spreading symptoms.
prevention: Mulch beneath plants to reduce soil splash.
Stake plants and maintain airflow.
Rotate crops and consider locally suitable resistant varieties.

Tomato Late Blight.description: Late blight, caused by Phytophthora infestans, can spread quickly and cause water-soaked brown lesions on leaves, stems, and fruit.
management: Seek prompt local confirmation if lesions spread rapidly.
Remove diseased foliage and manage affected crop residue.
Reduce leaf wetness using soil-level irrigation.
prevention: Inspect plants regularly, especially during wet weather.
Space and support plants for air movement.
Use healthy transplants and suitable resistant varieties.

Tomato Bacterial Spot.description: Bacterial spot causes small brown leaf spots, sometimes with yellow halos or holes, and can also damage fruit. Splashing water and handling spread it.
management: Remove visibly affected leaves and sanitize tools.
Keep leaves dry with drip or base watering.
Inspect nearby plants and obtain confirmation for severe symptoms.
prevention: Buy seed and transplants from reputable sources.
Do not save seed from affected plants.
Rotate crops, remove residue, and maintain plant spacing.

Tomato Leaf Mold.description: Leaf mold is a fungal disease favored by high humidity, especially under cover. Yellow patches above may correspond to olive-brown mold below the leaf.
management: Improve ventilation in greenhouses or covered growing areas.
Water at the base and reduce humidity around foliage.
Remove affected crop residue and clean supports and tools.
prevention: Space, stake, and prune plants to improve air circulation.
Use clean seed and transplants.
Consider resistant varieties after checking local suitability.

Maize Common Rust.description: Rust-coloured pustules on maize leaves may indicate common rust, a fungal disease. Similar rusts can look alike.
management: Inspect both leaf surfaces and monitor disease spread.
Use resistant maize hybrids; ask a local agronomist whether treatment is warranted.
prevention: Plan resistant hybrids for future planting.
Base any fungicide decision on confirmed disease, crop stage and local risk.

Maize Gray Leaf Spot.description: Gray leaf spot can produce rectangular grey or brown lesions limited by maize leaf veins. Humid conditions favour disease.
management: Scout lower and upper leaves and seek confirmation of rectangular lesions.
Use crop rotation and locally appropriate residue management.
prevention: Choose resistant hybrids.
Assess fungicide need with a local agronomist; an image score alone is insufficient.

Maize Northern Leaf Blight.description: Northern leaf blight can cause elongated, canoe-shaped lesions that become tan on maize leaves.
management: Inspect lesion shape and disease progression, especially before silking.
Seek local advice when symptoms spread rapidly.
prevention: Use resistant maize hybrids and rotate crops.
Manage infected residue where appropriate for local soil-conservation practices.

Potato Early Blight.description: Early blight may produce brown spots with concentric rings on potato leaves and lead to loss of foliage.
management: Scout affected foliage and confirm the cause before treatment.
Reduce prolonged leaf wetness and maintain balanced crop nutrition.
prevention: Rotate away from susceptible crops and manage infected residue.
Use healthy planting material and suitable spacing.

Potato Late Blight.description: Late blight may cause rapidly enlarging water-soaked or dark lesions on potato foliage and can also affect tubers.
management: Seek prompt local agricultural advice if late blight is suspected; it can spread quickly.
Avoid moving suspect infected plant material to other fields.
prevention: Plant certified healthy seed potatoes and eliminate volunteer plants and infected cull sources.
Monitor local disease warnings and follow locally approved management guidance.

Bell Pepper Bacterial Spot.description: Bacterial spot can cause water-soaked or brown spots on pepper foliage and may also damage fruit.
management: Avoid handling plants when leaves are wet and reduce overhead irrigation.
Seek confirmation before treatment; similar leaf spots have different causes.
prevention: Use disease-free seed or transplants and rotate susceptible crops.
Clean tools and manage infected crop residue.

Maize Healthy.description: Leaf patterns most closely match the model's healthy maize examples. This does not exclude pests, nutrient stress or unsupported diseases.
management: Continue regular scouting and locally appropriate crop care.
Seek agricultural advice if symptoms persist despite a healthy model match.
prevention: Use healthy planting material and clean tools.
Monitor the whole plant rather than relying on one leaf photo.

confidence_note: Confidence is the global softmax score among fourteen crop-condition classes, not diagnostic certainty. Crop selection does not verify plant identity. Field performance is not established; confirm important symptoms locally.
